title: Top Hosted Model + Workload Matrix (FP8/INT8 Benchmarking Sprint)
author: Rina Kobayashi
body:
## Purpose
This page defines the canonical **“top hosted”** model set and the benchmark **workload presets** used by the FP8/INT8 kernel benchmarking sprint.

The goal is to ensure results are:
- Representative of **hosted production traffic** (prompt lengths, streaming behavior, concurrency)
- Comparable across GPU SKUs and runtime commits
- Stable enough to gate regressions (see ADRs and thresholds)

This page is intentionally prescriptive. If you need to deviate, create a new preset and document the rationale.

---

## Scope
**In-scope:** Chat/completions serving paths (prefill + decode), streaming and non-streaming, mixed prompt lengths, scheduler pressure.

**Out-of-scope (for this matrix):** Embeddings-only workloads, reranking, tool-calling correctness behavior, multi-modal.

---

## Definitions
- **Prefill**: Time and compute to ingest prompt tokens and build initial KV cache.
- **Decode**: Autoregressive generation of output tokens.
- **TTFT (Time to First Token)**: From request start to first generated token (streaming) or first token available (non-streaming simulated).
- **TPOT (Time per Output Token)**: Avg (or distribution) time per generated token after first token.
- **Concurrency**: Number of in-flight requests to the runtime (client-side controlled in harness).
- **Workload preset**: Named combination of prompt distribution + decode settings + concurrency + streaming mode.

---

## “Top hosted” model set (bench targets)
The set below reflects models that (a) represent the majority of hosted chat/completions traffic, and (b) exercise different kernel/scheduler behaviors.

Notes:
- Exact model revisions are pinned in the benchmark config schema (see benchmark-lab config). This page defines the *families* and *serving shapes* we care about.
- If a model is unavailable on a given GPU SKU/region, mark the cell as **N/A** and record the reason in the results artifact.

### Model families and canonical variants
| ID | Model family | Canonical hosted variant (example) | Primary purpose in matrix | Known sensitivity areas |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | Llama family | Llama-3.x-Instruct (8B/70B class) | Balanced general chat; widely used baseline | Prefill at mid/long context; KV cache scaling behavior |
| M2 | Qwen family | Qwen2.x-Instruct (7B/72B class) | Strong multilingual + long context; different attention mix | Long context prefill; decode stability under batching |
| M3 | Mistral family | Mistral/Mixtral Instruct class | MoE-ish behavior / routing overhead; diverse shapes | Decode tail latency under mixed prompt lengths |

**Sizing guidance (for perf lab):**
- Run at least one **“small”** (7–10B class) and one **“large”** (70–72B class) per family where available.
- If constrained by capacity, prioritize: Llama small + Llama large + Qwen large + one Mistral/Mixtral representative.

Ownership:
- Model selection + updates: **Noah Patel** (runtime perf) + **Arjun Desai** (quant profiles)
- Quality sanity checks on prompt sets: **Jonas Weber**

---

## Prompt sets
Prompt sets are designed to hit:
- Short interactive chat (decode-heavy)
- Typical SaaS assistant prompts (mixed)
- Long context (prefill-heavy)
- “Spiky” prompts that historically trigger scheduler tail latency

### Prompt set catalog
| Prompt set ID | Name | Description | Source | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | chat_short | Short user messages and short system prompts | Curated synthetic, validated for token lengths | Used for decode-heavy benchmarks |
| P2 | chat_typical | Common assistant prompts (emails, summaries, Q&A) | Curated synthetic + lightly anonymized patterns | Representative default |
| P3 | chat_long_context | Long system + retrieved context + user question | Synthetic RAG-like | Used to stress prefill kernels and memory bandwidth |
| P4 | chat_mixed_spiky | Mixture of short + long prompts with bimodal distribution | Synthetic | Designed to amplify queueing and batching effects |

**Prompt content policy:** Prompt text lives in the benchmark repository artifact store; Confluence pages contain only summaries. Prompts must be non-customer-identifying.

---

## Sequence length distributions
We standardize prompt/output lengths at the *distribution* level to reduce overfitting to a single shape.

### Canonical token length bands
We define token bands used by the harness to sample prompts (or truncate/expand where defined by the prompt generator):
- **S (short):** 32–128 prompt tokens
- **M (medium):** 256–1,024 prompt tokens
- **L (long):** 2,048–8,192 prompt tokens
- **XL (xlong):** 16,384–64,000 prompt tokens (only for models configured for long context)

### Workload distributions (prompt length)
| Distribution ID | Band weights | Intended effect |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | 70% S, 25% M, 5% L | Interactive chat; decode-heavy |
| D2 | 25% S, 55% M, 20% L | Typical production mix |
| D3 | 10% S, 20% M, 70% L | Prefill-heavy; stresses attention/GEMM prefill |
| D4 | 50% S, 10% M, 40% L | “Spiky” mix; maximizes tail latency scenarios |
| D5 | 100% XL | Long-context prefill stress (gated; run only on long-context-enabled variants) |

### Output length targets
Output length is controlled via `max_new_tokens` and stopping behavior. We use two targets:
- **O1 (short output):** 64 tokens
- **O2 (medium output):** 256 tokens
- **O3 (long output):** 1,024 tokens (run selectively; expensive; used for decode efficiency)

**Stopping rule:** Use deterministic stop conditions (explicit stop sequences) in P1/P2 where feasible to reduce output-length variance. Otherwise enforce `max_new_tokens` hard cap.

---

## Decoding parameters (standard)
To make performance comparable, decoding parameters are fixed per workload preset.

### Default decoding parameters
| Parameter | Value | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| temperature | 0.7 | Representative of hosted defaults; avoids fully deterministic quirks |
| top_p | 0.9 | Common default |
| top_k | 0 (disabled) | Reduce implementation variance across backends |
| repetition_penalty | 1.0 | Avoid model-specific penalties affecting token distributions |
| presence_penalty | 0.0 | Keep stable |
| frequency_penalty | 0.0 | Keep stable |
| seed | 42 (fixed) | Stabilize sampling variance where supported |
| stop_sequences | workload-specific | Used to constrain runaway generations |

### Determinism mode for microbench/e2e
- **Microbench (kernel-level):** use deterministic settings where possible (temperature=0 where supported) to reduce divergence.
- **End-to-end serving:** use standard settings above; correctness guardrails cover drift.

---

## Streaming vs non-streaming modes
We test both modes because they stress different runtime behaviors:

- **Streaming:** TTFT and early-token scheduling are critical; scheduler interleaving matters.
- **Non-streaming:** Throughput and aggregate latency dominate; batching can be more aggressive.

### Standard response modes
| Mode ID | Mode | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| S0 | Non-streaming | Measure end-to-end latency and tokens/sec; client waits for completion |
| S1 | Streaming | Measure TTFT + TPOT; client consumes token stream; request remains in-flight longer |

---

## Concurrency levels (standard)
Concurrency is chosen to expose batching/scheduler behavior and tail latency.

### Concurrency presets
| Concurrency ID | In-flight requests | Use |
|---|---|---|
| C1 | 1 | Single-request baseline; microbench alignment |
| C2 | 8 | Light batching; typical low-traffic |
| C3 | 32 | Moderate load; exposes queueing |
| C4 | 64 | Heavy load; tail latency + backpressure |
| C5 | 128 | Stress; run selectively (large models or small GPUs may OOM or thrash) |

**Guideline:**
- For small models (7–10B), run up to C4 by default.
- For large models (70B+), default to C2/C3; add C4 only if stable on target GPU.

---

## Workload preset matrix (canonical)
These presets are the “golden set” for the sprint report and perf-canary. Each preset defines prompt distribution + output target + streaming mode + concurrency.

### Canonical workload presets
| Workload ID | Prompt set | Prompt distribution | Output target | Mode | Concurrency | Primary metrics | Why it exists |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| W1 | P1 chat_short | D1 | O1 | S1 Streaming | C2 | TTFT p50/p95, TPOT p50/p95 | Decode-heavy streaming baseline |
| W2 | P2 chat_typical | D2 | O2 | S1 Streaming | C3 | TTFT, TPOT, tokens/sec | Representative hosted traffic |
| W3 | P2 chat_typical | D2 | O2 | S0 Non-streaming | C3 | total latency, tokens/sec | Batch-friendly counterpart to W2 |
| W4 | P3 chat_long_context | D3 | O1 | S1 Streaming | C2 | TTFT p95, prefill time | Prefill stress + TTFT sensitivity |
| W5 | P4 chat_mixed_spiky | D4 | O1 | S1 Streaming | C4 | TTFT p95/p99, queue wait | Tail latency + scheduler stress |
| W6 | P3 chat_long_context | D5 | O1 | S0 Non-streaming | C1 | prefill tokens/sec, total latency | Long-context prefill micro-stress (selective) |
| W7 | P2 chat_typical | D2 | O3 | S0 Non-streaming | C2 | decode tokens/sec, TPOT | Decode efficiency under longer generations (selective) |

**Selectivity rules:**
- W6 runs only on long-context-enabled deployments and GPUs with sufficient memory.
- W7 runs on a subset of models (at least one per family) due to cost.

---

## Mapping: models x workloads (what we run)
This table defines the minimum run matrix for “top hosted” coverage.

Legend: ✅ required, ◻️ optional, ⛔ do not run (low signal or too expensive)

| Model family | Size class | W1 | W2 | W3 | W4 | W5 | W6 | W7 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Llama | small | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ◻️ | ◻️ |
| Llama | large | ◻️ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ◻️ | ◻️ |
| Qwen | small | ◻️ | ✅ | ✅ | ◻️ | ✅ | ⛔ | ◻️ |
| Qwen | large | ◻️ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ◻️ |
| Mistral/Mixtral | small | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ◻️ | ✅ | ⛔ | ◻️ |
| Mistral/Mixtral | large | ◻️ | ✅ | ✅ | ◻️ | ✅ | ⛔ | ◻️ |

**Rationale:**
- We always run W2/W3 for throughput comparability.
- We require at least one prefill-heavy workload (W4) per major long-context family.
- We require one tail-latency workload (W5) for scheduler + batching interactions.

---

## Quant modes for the matrix (how to apply)
Each model/workload is run under:
- **Q0:** FP16/BF16 baseline (control)
- **Q1:** FP8 (per ADR format/accumulation policy)
- **Q2:** INT8 (per quant profile compatibility notes)

Rules:
- If a model does not support FP8/INT8 end-to-end (partial coverage), run it but label results as **“partial quant”** and include fallback counts (requires kernel-selection logging).
- Any workload with correctness guardrail failure is recorded but excluded from “recommended defaults” until fixed.

---

## Benchmark harness configuration notes (for reproducibility)
These settings are part of the workload definition and must be recorded in results metadata:
- Runtime commit/version and build flags
- Model revision / tokenizer revision
- Max context length configuration (esp. for W6)
- KV cache type/config
- Scheduler policy preset and any overrides
- Batching settings (max batch size / max tokens in batch)
- Streaming implementation (chunk size / flush cadence)

**Warmup requirement:** Each (model, GPU, quant, workload) run must include warmup iterations; see methodology page for exact counts.

---

## Acceptance criteria for adding or changing a preset
To add or modify a workload preset:
1. Open a PR against benchmark-lab presets (include name, intent, and config).
2. Provide a one-paragraph justification: what production behavior it covers that current presets do not.
3. Run A/B on at least one GPU (A100 or H100) and one model family and show stability (variance within expected bounds).
4. Get sign-off from **Rina Kobayashi** (harness), **Noah Patel** (runtime perf), and **Jonas Weber** (eval sanity).

---

## Owner / on-call notes
- This page is owned by **Benchmark Harness** (Rina Kobayashi).
- For questions about “what is representative,” tag **Noah Patel**.
- For prompt-set or drift sensitivity concerns, tag **Jonas Weber** and **Arjun Desai**.

---

## Changelog
- 2025-10-11: Added W5 (chat_mixed_spiky) as required for tail latency; clarified D4 distribution and selectivity for W6/W7.
- 2025-10-03: Standardized decoding parameters and concurrency presets; aligned names with benchmark-lab schema.
- 2025-09-29: Initial publication (W1–W4 baseline set).
